correctness.rationale: For z=(x,a) in the unit sphere of the real l1-sum of X and ell1(Gamma), the dual norm is max(||f||,||c||_infinity)=1. Every slice norms at least one block: an X-only witness gives sup distance at least b+dc_X(x), while an almost-normed atomic coordinate gives at least 2(1-m). Since any given slice belongs to one of those cases, the min of both is a universal lower bound. Conversely an X-functional slice forces atomic norm <epsilon, yielding <=b+dc_X(x); a coordinate slice at |a_gamma| approaching m forces distance <=2(1-|a_gamma|), yielding <=2(1-m). Endpoint b=0 and m=1 are consistent; if X is Daugavet, dc_X(x)=1+||x|| so min is 2(1-m). An independent exact-rational check of 14,640 normalized signed integer vectors in ell1^d, 2<=d<=5, matched the known pure ell1 formula. CAVEAT: the proof’s ancillary assertion that a nonzero ell1 vector's infinity norm may fail to be attained is false—nonzero ell1 vectors attain that supremum; it is an unnecessary overcautious limit argument, not a premise or failure of the theorem. The KaTeX equation has an extra right brace; this must be corrected before publication.
